edges.description: A germ cell in the wrong place does not become a tumour by being there. What converts it is a return to pluripotency; no cited source shows the conversion happening in a human sacrococcygeal tumour, and the mouse work that does show it is testicular.
edges.source: Primordial Germ Cell Left in the Caudal Midline
edges.target: Epigenetic Reprogramming to a Pluripotent State

edges.description: A pluripotent cell differentiating in all three directions is what the mass is made of.
edges.source: Epigenetic Reprogramming to a Pluripotent State
edges.target: Tridermal Teratomatous Mass at the Sacrococcyx

edges.description: The mass as the finding: detected before birth in just over half of affected pregnancies in a national register; the study's abstract names no method of detection and does not say when the rest were found.
edges.source: Tridermal Teratomatous Mass at the Sacrococcyx

edges.description: A large, solid, highly vascular tumour is a low-resistance circuit in parallel with the fetus. The fetal heart compensates by raising output, and past a point it fails. This is the arm every prenatal predictor in this entry is trying to anticipate.
edges.source: Tridermal Teratomatous Mass at the Sacrococcyx
edges.target: High-Output Cardiac State from Tumour Vascular Steal

edges.description: In a Dutch series, internal tumour haemorrhage was among the commonest causes of early death and, like the other common causes, strongly associated with larger tumour size. The series reports the association with size, not how the tumour comes to bleed.
edges.source: Tridermal Teratomatous Mass at the Sacrococcyx

edges.description: Yolk sac tumour either present from the start and missed, or arising later within a mature teratoma. No cited source settles which, and the meta-analysis that raises the question names both possibilities without choosing.
edges.source: Tridermal Teratomatous Mass at the Sacrococcyx

edges.description: The tumour and its removal both act on the same small anatomical space, which carries the nerves and sphincters of bowel and bladder. No cited source separates the damage the tumour does from the damage the operation does, and of the variables the Dutch national study examined, its abstract reports only one as a risk factor: tumour size, for an unacceptable scar.
edges.source: Tridermal Teratomatous Mass at the Sacrococcyx

edges.description: An enlarged placenta accompanies the high-output state, alongside hydrops and cardiomegaly. The review groups all three as factors associated with cardiac failure, which is the relation this edge draws; it does not say which of them produces which, so the edge runs through unknown intermediates rather than recording a measured sequence.
edges.source: High-Output Cardiac State from Tumour Vascular Steal

edges.description: The fatal end of this arm. The register reports the outcome without attributing each death to a mechanism, so the edge is drawn through unknown intermediates: high-output failure and hydrops are the route the other cited sources describe, not one this register measures.
edges.source: High-Output Cardiac State from Tumour Vascular Steal

edges.description: The decompensated end of the high-output state, and the point at which fetal intervention is considered.
edges.source: High-Output Cardiac State from Tumour Vascular Steal

edges.description: The heart's response to the sustained output demand, and a predictor of poor outcome in its own right.
edges.source: High-Output Cardiac State from Tumour Vascular Steal

edges.description: Excess amniotic fluid accompanies the severe form. One cited series states, in its review of the literature, that the raised cardiac output contributes to it, without saying how; a systematic review found it much commoner among non-survivors managed without intervention.
edges.source: High-Output Cardiac State from Tumour Vascular Steal

edges.description: Delivery is earlier when the fetus is compromised, and earlier delivery is itself what several series find associated with death. One cited series names a route in its review of the literature: the raised output contributes to polyhydramnios, which can lead to preterm birth by distending the uterus. Whether early delivery causes the deaths or marks the fetuses already failing, the cohort data quoted here cannot say.
edges.source: High-Output Cardiac State from Tumour Vascular Steal

edges.description: In one case the mother's illness began shortly after the fetus showed early signs of right heart failure, before overt hydrops, and resolved after delivery; the same report says the syndrome is usually associated with severe fetal hydrops. A second case report's discussion cites earlier work linking the arteriovenous shunts of a large tumour to cardiac failure, placentomegaly, hydrops and the syndrome, and says the placenta has been suggested as its source, because ending the pregnancy resolves the maternal oedema. No cited source demonstrates the mechanism, so the edge runs through unknown intermediates.
edges.source: High-Output Cardiac State from Tumour Vascular Steal

edges.description: High-output cardiac failure is one of the commonest causes of early death, with internal tumour haemorrhage and bleeding at operation.
edges.source: High-Output Cardiac State from Tumour Vascular Steal

edges.description: Death after birth from bleeding. In the Dutch series internal tumour haemorrhage was among the commonest causes of early death; nine children died within 27 days of birth, seven of the deaths related to tumour haemorrhage, circulatory failure or both, and haemorrhagic deaths, which the abstract does not split by source, were almost 70% of the neonatal mortality. Neither of the last two figures is specific to bleeding into the tumour.
The marker the malignant component secretes, and the thing surveillance measures.

Recurrence with malignant histology, which is what makes recurrence matter. It can be very late: many occur within one to six years and some as long as twenty years after diagnosis; no cited source gives the fraction in that window.

The scar is left by the resection this node's consequences follow from, not by the mass itself. It sits here because the Dutch national study counts it alongside the bowel and bladder sequelae as one of the three long-term problems that affect quality of life.
Soiling or involuntary bowel movements after resection, in about a fifth of long-term survivors.
Reported by just under a third of long-term survivors.
The commonest single bowel complaint in the Dutch national questionnaire study, at 17%.

Functional sequelae are reported more often after resection of a tumour with a large intrapelvic extension, and abnormal bladder function differs by Altman type; the entry places injury to the pelvic and sacral nerves between the tumour's extent and that dysfunction, a step these abstracts do not measure. A 2022 MRI series restates tumour compression or infiltration of the sacral nerves among the tumour's complications, without measuring it. The Dutch national questionnaire study found no long-term sequela associated with Altman type. The mass effect's own edges to the two incontinence phenotypes carry that study's figures; this route carries that restatement and the factors that go with dysfunction.

Abnormal bladder function differed by Altman type in a 2023 systematic review, lowest in type I (18%) and highest in type IV (60%), with types II and III at 37.7% and 32.4% (p = 0.007), and adverse urological outcomes were commoner in patients who needed reoperation and with immature or malignant tumours; in a Swedish series univariate analysis found urinary tract dysfunction correlated with immature histology, and the abstract reports only low gestational age as an independent predictor. A 2022 MRI series restates nerve compression leading to incontinence. The Dutch national questionnaire study found neither Altman type nor histopathology to be a risk factor for any long-term sequela, urinary incontinence included. These are factors that go with dysfunction; no cited source measures the nerve injury itself.

Anorectal dysfunction after resection; in the 2020 series the patients with functional disorders, who by the abstract's counts all had anorectal dysfunction, had larger tumours, surgical injury to the pelvic organs and immature or malignant histology, and in a Swedish series bowel dysfunction correlated with tumour size on univariate analysis. A 2022 MRI series restates nerve compression leading to incontinence. The 2023 systematic review found that bowel dysfunction had no significant association with tumour characteristics. These are factors that go with dysfunction; no cited source measures the nerve injury itself.
Leg weakness from sciatic nerve palsy, in 2 of 27 children in a 1990 series.
The syndrome can force delivery: a hydropic fetus with the tumour was delivered at 27 weeks for it.

edges.description: The only cited source that shows the reprogramming step happening, with a named chromatin mechanism and both a loss-of-function and a rescue arm.
edges.limitations: The tumours are testicular, not sacrococcygeal, and they arise in one inbred strain. No cited source reports a sacrococcygeal teratoma model in any species, so the step this link supplies is transferred across both organ and genetic background.
edges.target: Epigenetic Reprogramming to a Pluripotent State

edges.description: These strains do form germ cell teratomas, so they reach the node; they reach it in the wrong organ. Four of them gave ovarian teratomas where testicular ones were expected, and the authors call that result surprising. The paper also states, as background, that Dnd1-mutant mice show germ cell loss rather than teratoma, which reads against the other cited mouse paper reporting that Dnd1 mutation enhances teratoma formation in 129/Sv. The strain behind the germ cell loss sentence is not given in the cached abstract, so this entry cannot say whether the two results are a genuine disagreement or two strains behaving differently.
edges.limitations: Neither result is in the caudal midline and neither is in a human, so the site this disease is defined by is outside the model. The organ the strain was built for is not the organ it produced.
edges.target: Epigenetic Reprogramming to a Pluripotent State

edges.description: In follow-up for recurrence, a readout of the malignant yolk sac component. In a systematic review its sensitivity for malignant recurrence was 96%; the review cautions that its sensitivity to detect recurrence could be overestimated, because levels are mainly reported in patients with raised levels or at recurrence. In the Dutch cohort the level rose in malignant recurrences but did not predict mature or immature recurrence, and a normal value did not rule recurrence out.

nodes.description: Needle drainage of excess amniotic fluid. It treats a consequence of the tumour, not the tumour: a 2024 systematic review of fetal surgery left it out because its intention is not to reduce tumour size. In a 2004 series the indications given for cyst aspiration and amnioreduction together were maternal discomfort, preterm labour and prevention of tumour rupture at delivery, and the series' authors call amnioreduction, cyst aspiration and surgical debulking potentially life-saving.

evidence.reference_title: Sacrococcygeal teratoma: prenatal assessment, fetal intervention, and outcome.
evidence.snippet: Fetal intervention included cyst aspiration (n = 6), amnioreduction (n = 3), amnioinfusion (n = 1), and open fetal surgical resection (n = 4).

evidence.reference_title: Sacrococcygeal teratoma: prenatal assessment, fetal intervention, and outcome.
evidence.snippet: Amnioreduction, cyst aspiration, and surgical debulking are potentially life-saving interventions.

evidence.reference_title: Perinatal Outcomes of Intrauterine Interventions for Fetal Sacrococcygeal Teratoma Based on Different Surgical Techniques-A Systematic Review.
evidence.snippet: Articles and studies that described procedures such as tumor cyst puncture, amnioreduction, and fetal transfusion during SCT management were excluded, as their intention was not to reduce tumor size.

nodes.description: A late consequence, reported at a median age of nearly ten years. Later reports give bowel dysfunction more broadly, without separating incontinence from other complaints: 19% of index cases in a 2023 systematic review of published studies, 36% in a Swedish series and 20.7% (anorectal dysfunction) in a 2020 single-centre series.

evidence.reference_title: Long-term functional sequelae of sacrococcygeal teratoma: a national study in The Netherlands.
evidence.snippet: Long-term functional sequelae after resection of sacrococcygeal teratoma (SCT) are relatively common.

evidence.reference_title: Long-term functional sequelae of sacrococcygeal teratoma: a national study in The Netherlands.
evidence.snippet: There were 46% who reported impaired bowel function and/or urinary incontinence (9% involuntary bowel movements, 13% soiling, 17% constipation), and 31% urinary incontinence.

evidence.reference_title: Long-term functional outcomes of sacrococcygeal teratoma - A systematic review of published studies exploring 'real world' outcomes.
evidence.snippet: Bowel dysfunction was evident in 19% index cases and constipation in 26% with no significant association(s) with tumour characteristics.

evidence.reference_title: Functional outcome and health-related quality of life in patients with sacrococcygeal teratoma - a Swedish multicenter study.
evidence.snippet: Bowel dysfunction was reported by 36% and urinary tract dysfunction by 46% of the patients.

evidence.reference_title: Long-term functional outcome of sacrococcygeal teratoma after resection in neonates and infants: a single-center experience.
evidence.snippet: Anorectal dysfunction, urologic dysfunction, and lower-extremity motor disorders occurred in 6 (20.7%), 4 (13.8%), and 3 (10.3%) patients, respectively.

nodes.description: When the tumour is large (more than 5 to 10 cm across) or highly vascular, vaginal birth is not recommended because of a higher risk of rupture and bleeding. The mode of delivery is chosen case by case; in a 2025 single-centre series 8 of the 9 delivered fetuses, two of them not detected before birth, were born by caesarean section, and the ninth by a spontaneous precipitous vaginal delivery. A tumour that is large for the fetus's weight also predicts a higher-risk maternal operation: a 2019 single-centre study counted open fetal surgery, classical caesarean delivery and EXIT as such operations, and a tumour volume to fetal weight ratio above 0.12 at or before 24 weeks predicted one.
nodes.id: Caesarean section for a large or vascular tumour

evidence.reference_title: Sacrococcygeal teratoma - prognosis based on prenatal ultrasound diagnosis, single-center experience and literature review.
evidence.snippet: The mode of delivery is selected individually.

evidence.reference_title: Sacrococcygeal teratoma - prognosis based on prenatal ultrasound diagnosis, single-center experience and literature review.
evidence.snippet: Among the nine delivered fetuses (including two cases not detected prenatally), eight patients (88.9%) underwent cesarean section, while one case (11.1%) resulted in spontaneous precipitous vaginal delivery.

evidence.reference_title: High Tumor Volume to Fetal Weight Ratio Is Associated with Worse Fetal Outcomes and Increased Maternal Risk in Fetuses with Sacrococcygeal Teratoma.
evidence.snippet: Increased maternal operative risk included cases necessitating open fetal surgery, classical cesarean delivery, or ex utero intrapartum treatment (EXIT).

evidence.reference_title: High Tumor Volume to Fetal Weight Ratio Is Associated with Worse Fetal Outcomes and Increased Maternal Risk in Fetuses with Sacrococcygeal Teratoma.
evidence.snippet: ROC analysis revealed that at <=24 weeks, TFR > 0.095 was predictive of poor fetal outcome and TFR > 0.12 was predictive of increased maternal operative risk.

nodes.description: The heart enlarging under a sustained output demand, and one of the two potential risk factors for poor outcome that an 84-fetus Dutch national cohort identifies. Its abstract reports no multivariate analysis; the three-centre series that ran one found no factor independent, while two growth series each found one growth measure that was.

evidence.reference_title: Factors associated with poor outcome in fetuses prenatally diagnosed with sacrococcygeal teratoma.
evidence.snippet: Potential risk factors for poor outcome were fetal hydrops and cardiomegaly.

nodes.description: The definitive treatment, done after birth in most patients. Completeness is what matters: positive margins raise the recurrence rate about tenfold in one series, and incomplete resection is named as a risk factor for recurrence by a review. The coccyx is removed with the tumour: two series report doing so in their own patients, and a review names failure to remove it among the primary drivers of recurrence.

evidence.reference_title: Malignant transformation in sacrococcygeal teratoma and in presacral teratoma associated with Currarino syndrome: a comparative study.
evidence.snippet: In SCT, malignancy and recurrence risk are high.

evidence.reference_title: Malignant transformation in sacrococcygeal teratoma and in presacral teratoma associated with Currarino syndrome: a comparative study.
evidence.snippet: Therefore, early and complete resection is mandatory.

evidence.reference_title: A single-center experience of magnetic resonance imaging findings of fetal sacrococcygeal teratomas.
evidence.snippet: Treatment is with surgical excision inclusive of coccygectomy with additional chemotherapy for malignant ones.

evidence.reference_title: Sacrococcygeal teratoma - prognosis based on prenatal ultrasound diagnosis, single-center experience and literature review.
evidence.snippet: Coccyx removal is indicated as part of the surgical treatment, which prevents local recurrence

evidence.reference_title: Sacrococcygeal teratoma - prognosis based on prenatal ultrasound diagnosis, single-center experience and literature review.
evidence.snippet: This approach was applied to all operated newborns in our group.

evidence.reference_title: Antenatal and Postnatal Management of Sacrococcygeal Teratoma.
evidence.snippet: Surgical management relies on multidisciplinary perinatal planning and includes complete oncologic resection with coccygectomy.

evidence.reference_title: Antenatal and Postnatal Management of Sacrococcygeal Teratoma.
evidence.snippet: Incomplete resection, tumor spillage, failure to remove the coccyx, and immature/malignant tumor elements are the primary drivers of recurrence.

evidence.reference_title: Malignant benign neonatal sacrococcygeal teratoma.
evidence.snippet: The initial surgical removal of the SCT (including the coccyx) was carried out during the first 7 days of life.

nodes.description: The commonest single bowel complaint in the Dutch national questionnaire study, at 17%. Other reports give higher figures: 26% of index cases in a 2023 systematic review of published studies, and 39% in a Scottish national cohort, where it was the commonest bowel complaint.

evidence.reference_title: Long-term functional sequelae of sacrococcygeal teratoma: a national study in The Netherlands.
evidence.snippet: A large proportion of the patients with SCT have problems with defecation, urinary incontinence, or a cosmetically unacceptable scar that affects QoL.

evidence.reference_title: Long-term functional outcomes of sacrococcygeal teratoma - A systematic review of published studies exploring 'real world' outcomes.
evidence.snippet: Bowel dysfunction was evident in 19% index cases and constipation in 26% with no significant association(s) with tumour characteristics.

evidence.reference_title: The long-term outcome of patients diagnosed with sacrococcygeal teratoma in childhood. A study of a national cohort.
evidence.snippet: Abnormal bowel function was noted in 42% of patients, with constipation being the commonest complaint (39%) with no obvious predictive features at presentation.

evidence.reference_title: Long-term functional sequelae of sacrococcygeal teratoma: a national study in The Netherlands.
evidence.snippet: There were 46% who reported impaired bowel function and/or urinary incontinence (9% involuntary bowel movements, 13% soiling, 17% constipation), and 31% urinary incontinence.

nodes.description: Two of every five respondents in the Dutch national study rated the scar cosmetically unacceptable. That is the highest single complaint the study reports, although a larger share, 46 percent, reported impaired bowel function or urinary incontinence as a composite. It is a consequence of the resection rather than of the tumour, which is why it is wired from the mass-effect node and not from the mass itself, and it is recorded because the same study found it affects quality of life.

evidence.reference_title: Long-term functional sequelae of sacrococcygeal teratoma: a national study in The Netherlands.
evidence.snippet: In 40%, the scar was cosmetically unacceptable.

nodes.description: The classical teratoma mouse. Loss of DND1 drastically raises teratoma incidence, and the mechanism is worked out: DND1 suppresses a microRNA that inhibits EZH2, so its loss lowers H3K27me3 at a cell-cycle gene and the germ cells reprogramme.

The marker of the malignant component, and the basis of surveillance. Interpreting it in an infant is the hard part: alpha-fetoprotein is enormous at birth and halves every five days through the first four weeks, then settles: between day 180 and day 720 the cited reference study reports no further decline, and adult levels are still not reached by two years.

evidence.reference_title: Diagnostic accuracy of serum alpha-fetoprotein levels in diagnosing recurrent sacrococcygeal teratoma: A systematic review.
evidence.snippet: Fifteen studies (613 patients, 121 recurrences) were included and these mainly described serum AFP levels in patients with recurrent SCT (n = 111); 83 (75%) patients with recurrent SCT had elevated serum AFP levels.

evidence.reference_title: Alpha 1-fetoprotein (AFP) reference values in infants up to 2 years of age.
evidence.snippet: At birth mean serum AFP levels were 41,687 ng/ml in 256 term babies and 158,125 ng/ml in 90 premature babies born before the 37th gestational week, excluding samples from children with factors known to be associated with AFP elevation.

nodes.description: The misplaced germ cell reacquires the capacity to make all three germ layers. The bound process is stem cell population maintenance, which is the nearest GO has: searching GO for reprogramming and for pluripotency returns nothing, and this term's own definition ends by allowing that stem cells may arise de novo from other cell types. In mouse testicular teratoma this step has a named mechanism - loss of DND1 lowers EZH2 and H3K27me3 at a cell-cycle gene, and the germ cells reprogramme to pluripotent stem cells - and that is a different organ and a different strain background from this disease.
nodes.id: Epigenetic Reprogramming to a Pluripotent State

Four of them gave ovarian teratomas where testicular ones were expected, and the authors call that result surprising. The strain behind the germ cell loss sentence is not given in the cached abstract, so this entry cannot say whether the two results are a genuine disagreement or two strains behaving differently.

evidence.snippet: In addition, Ezh2 expression or Ccnd1 deficiency repressed the reprogramming of PGCs into pluripotent stem cells, which mimicked the conversion of embryonic germ cells into teratoma-forming cells.

evidence.reference_title: Comprehensive genetic analysis of pediatric germ cell tumors identifies potential drug targets.
evidence.snippet: Teratomas had higher expression of ectodermal genes, suggesting a tridermal nature.

nodes.description: Interrupting the tumour's blood supply before birth, to reverse the high-output state rather than to remove the tumour. The first report of it is also the clearest statement of its limit: ablating most of the tumour mass was unnecessary and killed two of four fetuses. In a 2024 systematic review survival was 45.8% (22 of 48) after percutaneous procedures as a group and 12 of 18 (67%) after radiofrequency ablation itself, against 71.0% (66 of 93) without intervention; in a 2011 cohort it was 6 of 8 after fetal intervention (radiofrequency ablation in six, shunting alone in two) against 14 of 14 without, an outcome the authors call similar despite the treated fetuses' worse prognostic features. The groups are not alike: in the review fetal intervention is indicated for fetuses with hydrops or cardiac dysfunction, and hydrops and cardiac failure were rarer without it; in the 2011 cohort the treated fetuses' tumours were larger, rapidly growing and more often vascular, with associated polyhydramnios or cardiomegaly. The review says it could not evaluate the effectiveness of fetal surgery of any type against no fetal intervention.
nodes.id: Fetal radiofrequency ablation of the feeding vessels

evidence.reference_title: Radiofrequency ablation of human fetal sacrococcygeal teratoma.
evidence.snippet: Ablation of a majority of the tumor tissue in sacrococcygeal teratoma is not necessary and proved fatal in two instances.

evidence.reference_title: Minimally invasive therapy for fetal sacrococcygeal teratoma: case series and systematic review of the literature.
evidence.snippet: Including our cases, six of 20 hydropic fetuses survived after minimally invasive therapy (30%).

evidence.reference_title: Perinatal Outcomes of Intrauterine Interventions for Fetal Sacrococcygeal Teratoma Based on Different Surgical Techniques-A Systematic Review.
evidence.snippet: The survival rate was 56.2% in OS, 45.8% in PI (p = 0.568), and 71.0% in NI patients.

evidence.reference_title: Perinatal outcome of sacrococcygeal teratoma.
evidence.snippet: Tumors of cases undergoing in utero intervention were larger with rapidly growing, more frequently vascular, and with associated polyhydramnios or cardiomegaly.

evidence.reference_title: Perinatal outcome of sacrococcygeal teratoma.
evidence.snippet: The neonatal survival rate was 6/8 for the prenatal intervention group and 14/14 for the nonintervention group.

evidence.reference_title: Perinatal outcome of sacrococcygeal teratoma.
evidence.snippet: Fetuses with SCT undergoing in utero intervention have worse prognostic features, yet their neonatal outcome is similar to those of fetuses not requiring intervention.

evidence.snippet: The survival rates of each percutaneous intervention were 39% (laser ablation: 9/23), 67% (RFA: 12/18), 20% (alcohol sclerosis: 1/5), and 0% (coiling: 0/1 and thermocoagulation: 0/1) (p = 0.160).

evidence.reference_title: Perinatal Outcomes of Intrauterine Interventions for Fetal Sacrococcygeal Teratoma Based on Different Surgical Techniques-A Systematic Review.
evidence.snippet: Our study did not aim to compare outcomes between patients submitted to fetal interventions and those with prenatal expectant management in fetuses with SCT, since fetal interventions are indicated for severe forms of SCT when hydrops or fetal cardiac dysfunction is present, while prenatal expectant management was performed in fetuses with SCT without those complications.

evidence.reference_title: Perinatal Outcomes of Intrauterine Interventions for Fetal Sacrococcygeal Teratoma Based on Different Surgical Techniques-A Systematic Review.
evidence.snippet: We identified 16 cases of open fetal surgery (OS), 48 cases of percutaneous fetal intervention (PI), and 93 NI patients.

evidence.reference_title: Perinatal Outcomes of Intrauterine Interventions for Fetal Sacrococcygeal Teratoma Based on Different Surgical Techniques-A Systematic Review.
evidence.snippet: The rates of SCT complications, including fetal hydrops and fetal cardiac failure, were also lower without fetal intervention.

evidence.snippet: Among the remaining 22 cases, in utero interventions were performed in eight, including radiofrequency ablation (RFA) in four, shunt operations in two, RFA plus cyst aspiration in one, and RFA with subsequent shunt operation in one.

evidence.snippet: Therefore, our study was not able to evaluate the effectiveness of fetal surgery (any type) compared to fetuses without fetal intervention.

nodes.description: Bleeding into the tumour. With high-output failure and bleeding at operation it is one of the commonest causes of early death, and all three are strongly associated with larger tumours. The Dutch series that reports this gives risk factors for haemorrhagic death - prematurity, a tumour volume above 1000 cm3 and emergency operation - and its abstract does not split haemorrhagic deaths by source, so those risk factors are not shown to be specific to bleeding into the tumour.

evidence.reference_title: Hemorrhage is the most common cause of neonatal mortality in patients with sacrococcygeal teratoma.
evidence.snippet: High-output cardiac failure, internal tumor hemorrhage and perioperative bleeding were the most common causes of early death and were all strongly associated with larger tumor sizes.

evidence.reference_title: Significant Clinical Manifestations in Ballantyne Syndrome, after a Case Report and Literature Review: Recognizing Preeclampsia as a Differential Diagnosis.
evidence.snippet: In our case the histologic examination of the tumor demonstrated signs of bleeding; nevertheless the presence of an arteriovenous shunt was not examined.

evidence.reference_title: Hemorrhage is the most common cause of neonatal mortality in patients with sacrococcygeal teratoma.
evidence.snippet: Risk factors for hemorrhagic mortality were prematurity, tumor volume>1000cm3 and performance of an emergency operation.

nodes.description: Combined ventricular output above 625 mL/min/kg with abnormal Doppler or echocardiographic findings is the definition one series used. Cardiomegaly, abnormal venous preload indices and umbilical venous pulsation are the signs; hydrops is the end of it.
nodes.id: High-Output Cardiac State from Tumour Vascular Steal

evidence.reference_title: Prenatal solid tumor volume index: novel prenatal predictor of adverse outcome in sacrococcygeal teratoma.
evidence.snippet: Outcomes measured were survival, hydrops or high cardiac output state, defined as a combined ventricular output of >625 mL/min/kg with abnormal Doppler or echocardiogram findings.

evidence.reference_title: Sonographic prognostic factors in prenatal diagnosis of SCT.
evidence.snippet: The most important prognostic criteria were cardiomegaly, fetal hydrops, and increased preload indexes of the fetal venous system as sign of fetal heart failure.

nodes.description: The decompensated end of the high-output state, and a strong reported predictor of poor outcome at an odds ratio of 21 in one cohort - though a cited growth-velocity study reports a higher odds ratio for a different measure, and one cited review finds no survival effect for hydrops at all, which the entry records as an open disagreement rather than resolving.

evidence.reference_title: Factors associated with poor outcome in fetuses prenatally diagnosed with sacrococcygeal teratoma.
evidence.snippet: Potential risk factors for poor outcome were the presence of fetal hydrops (OR: 21.0, CI: 2.6-275.1, p = 0.012) and cardiomegaly (OR: 10.3, CI: 1.9-55.8, p = 0.011).

evidence.reference_title: Perinatal Outcomes of Intrauterine Interventions for Fetal Sacrococcygeal Teratoma Based on Different Surgical Techniques-A Systematic Review.
evidence.snippet: In our evaluation, we determined that the presence of fetal hydrops and cardiac failure had no significant impact on survival in SCT cases.

nodes.description: Carboplatin, etoposide and bleomycin, for malignant germ cell tumour. The regimen was developed across germ cell tumour sites and four of its 21 patients had sacrococcygeal primaries, so this row records a regimen used in this disease rather than one tested in it.

evidence.reference_title: 'JEB'--a carboplatin based regimen for malignant germ cell tumours in children.
evidence.snippet: Primary sites were: testis (6), ovary (8), sacrococcyx (4), pineal gland (2) and vagina (1).

evidence.reference_title: 'JEB'--a carboplatin based regimen for malignant germ cell tumours in children.
evidence.snippet: It appears to have comparable efficacy to cisplatin-based regimens but with much less nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity and avoids the use of alkylating agents and anthracyclines.

nodes.description: Leg weakness at follow-up: lower-extremity motor disorders, not further specified, in 3 of 29 patients (10.3%) of a 2020 single-centre series after resection, and weakness of the legs from sciatic nerve palsy in 2 of 27 children of a 1990 series.

evidence.reference_title: Long-term functional outcome of sacrococcygeal teratoma after resection in neonates and infants: a single-center experience.
evidence.snippet: Anorectal dysfunction, urologic dysfunction, and lower-extremity motor disorders occurred in 6 (20.7%), 4 (13.8%), and 3 (10.3%) patients, respectively.

nodes.description: A preeclampsia-like illness in the mother, defined by fetal hydrops with placental and maternal oedema. In one case it began shortly after the fetus showed right heart failure, placentomegaly and polyhydramnios, before overt hydrops, which the authors set against the syndrome's usual association with severe fetal hydrops, and it resolved after delivery. A review of the tumour's management names it among the potentially lethal conditions a tumour can precipitate; with fetal hydrops it carries a grave prognosis, and it can force delivery.

nodes.description: Resection of the tumour in utero for a fetus in progressive high-output failure. The field has moved away from it towards the minimally invasive techniques above, and the cited survival figures do not separate the two by much. Survival after open surgery was 56.2% (9 of 16) in a 2024 systematic review, against 71.0% (66 of 93) without intervention. The review reports survival as significantly higher without intervention than in the cohorts treated by fetal surgery, without a p-value for that comparison and without saying whether it holds for open surgery alone, but says it did not aim to compare the two, because fetal intervention is indicated for the severe forms with hydrops or cardiac dysfunction, and that it could not evaluate the effectiveness of fetal surgery of any type against no fetal intervention.

nodes.description: The consequences that outlast the tumour. In the Dutch national questionnaire study of long-term survivors, nearly half reported impaired bowel function or urinary incontinence and 40% an unacceptable scar. Its authors conclude that clinical variables cannot clearly identify the patients at higher risk; on univariate analysis the one variable its abstract reports as a risk factor for any of them is tumour size above 500 cm3, for the scar. A single-centre series' review of the literature reports that the complications listed in one passage, early and late and mostly obstructive and bowel problems, are commoner in tumours with a larger intrapelvic component; that passage does not list incontinence or the scar; the series' introduction names incontinence and aesthetic concerns among long-term complications without tying them to the intrapelvic part.

nodes.description: Injury to the pelvic and sacral nerves. A 2022 MRI series restates tumour compression or infiltration of the sacral nerves among the tumour's complications, and a 1990 series attributes leg weakness to sciatic nerve palsy without saying what caused the palsy. The operation as a second cause is the entry's inference: none of the sources cited on this node names a surgical nerve injury, and the 2020 series' surgical injury is to the pelvic organs. The other cited sources give associations rather than a measured mechanism: functional sequelae were commoner after resecting large intrapelvic tumours by an abdominoperineal approach (67% in the 1990 series); in a 2020 single-centre series the patients with functional disorders had a low 1-minute Apgar score, larger tumours needing abdominosacral resection, surgical injury to the pelvic organs and immature or malignant histology; and a 2023 systematic review associates higher Altman type, unfavourable tumour biology and reoperation with poor function. The Dutch national questionnaire study found neither Altman type nor histopathology to be a risk factor for any long-term sequela.

nodes.description: An enlarged placenta, which the cited meta-analysis groups with cardiomegaly and fetal hydrops as a factor associated with cardiac failure. That is why it sits beside hydrops under the high-output node rather than as an independent lesion. The review gives no frequency, so this row carries none, and it reports association without direction, so the edge is drawn through unknown intermediates. In one case of mirror syndrome it appeared with right heart failure and polyhydramnios before overt hydrops, and in another the placenta was grossly oedematous, at 1,280 g, with marked hydropic change of the villi.

In one centre's series 9 of 11 fetuses delivered this way survived and none died of prematurity; the authors, reporting favourable outcomes in the absence of hydrops before 27 weeks or tumour rupture in utero, say their single-centre experience supports pre-emptive delivery for selected cases.

readouts.interpretation: In follow-up for recurrence, a readout of the malignant yolk sac component. In a systematic review its sensitivity for malignant recurrence was 96%; the review cautions that its sensitivity to detect recurrence could be overestimated, because levels are mainly reported in patients with raised levels or at recurrence. In the Dutch cohort the level rose in malignant recurrences but did not predict mature or immature recurrence, and a normal value did not rule recurrence out.
